project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will build capacity for telemedicine services to better meet the medical and behavioral health care needs of low-income and underserved patients. Idaho Primary Care Association (IPCA) will provide training and technical assistance to increase the use and functionality of telemedicine and distance learning within participating project sites. It will expand Medication Assisted Treatment (MAT) to address the opioid epidemic. It will increase access to behavioral health in primary care settings. And, it will also provide ongoing staff support to retain physicians and advance practice clinicians in rural and frontier communities and offer high-quality continuing education for rural providers.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist rural small and emerging private business enterprise located within 10 counties in South Western Idaho to reach a degree of business preparedness with the goal of obtaining financing through a variety of private and public business loan programs, including the USDA Business and Industry Guaranteed Loan program. funding_code: (COMB LOAN & GRANT) WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to increase the supply of water available to the Franklin Water System, which serves 641 residents. The city owns the water rights to two springs, but over the years it has been unable to get water from them due to the degradation of the piping system. Water storage and spring boxes will be rehabilitated, and approximately two miles of pipe to connect the springs to the water system will be replaced. This project will also add two backup wells. The project will provide the citys residents and businesses with reliable water quantity and quality. Additional funding includes $900,000 from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, a $500,000 Community Development Block Grant, $45,000 from Idaho Department of Environmental Quality planning grant, and a $45,000 applicant contribution.
